title: Tight Security of r-Round KACSP Beyond Three Rounds
summary: The tight security analysis is established only for 3KACSP; whether its bound generalizes to single-permutation KACSP constructions with more than three rounds remains unresolved.

formal_statement.body: Prove or refute that $r$-round KACSP security is $\Theta\!\left(2^{rn/(r+1)}\right)$ in the random-permutation model. The tight security analysis established for the 3-round key-alternating cipher with a single permutation (3KACSP) applies only to the three-round setting; it remains unresolved whether this analysis and its tight security bound can be generalized to key-alternating cipher with a single permutation constructions using more than three rounds, namely an $r$-round KACSP for $r>3$.

scope.domain: Security analysis of r-round key-alternating block ciphers using a single permutation in the random-permutation model.
parameters: n: parameter in the claimed security exponent
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether the tight analysis and bound extend to the single-permutation r-round KACSP for more than three rounds, namely r > 3, or can be refuted.

citations.label: Tight Security Analysis of 3-Round Key-Alternating Cipher with A Single Permutation

progress.summary: The source establishes the tight analysis for 3KACSP and presents the analogous r-round security bound as a conjecture in the random-permutation model. The extension to more than three rounds is left open.
citation_labels: Yusai Wu et al., Tight Security Analysis of 3-Round Key-Alternating Cipher with A Single Permutation
